articles.title: Lava Crack
articles.summary: Broad cooling plates with thin bright fissure lines between, mostly smooth with sharp glowing cracks. Reads as a fine crackle web across the panel; plates are big and quiet, so only a faint cracked-glaze impression survives.
articles.what: Cooling lava plates with bright glowing fissures between Up close: Hairline web of thin curving cracks forming large irregular plates 50-100 px across, like cooled lava or dry mud, each crack a thread-thin bright or dark line. Barely visible on satin; on metal the web shows in the highlight as fine bright seams and in the dim zone as dark cracks. From a distance: Reads as a fine crackle web across the panel; plates are big and quiet, so only a faint cracked-glaze impression survives. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Organic & Natural (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, hood, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Organic & Natural", or search for "Lava Crack".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: big plates need open panels
Best on metallic bases where the seams show
Numbers keep their colour; thin cracks may cross them faintly but legibility is fine.
Almost nothing: a faint hairline or two in the highlight
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic.
pitfalls: Not a glowing orange lava colour: it adds no colour, only thin seam lines in the shine
Not Voronoi cell tiles: lines are thin and wandering, not a bordered tile grid
Avoid: chrome bases that hide the thin fissures, tiny panels where plates crop awkwardly.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.goal: Layer Lava Crack over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Snake Scales
articles.summary: Soft elongated oval scales in offset rows, gentle convex specular peak near top, duller edges; subtle, low-contrast reptile sheen. Disappears completely; the surface looks like smooth satin or metal with at most a faint fine grain.
articles.what: Reptile scale array — elongated oval scales in offset rows, specular peak near scale center-top (convex surface), lower metallic at scale edges, overlap regions roughness Up close: Rows of tiny chevron-like specks, only a few pixels each, staggered in offset rows like very fine scales. Inside the highlight they show as a faint dotted bright pattern on a smooth ground; outside it they nearly disappear. From a distance: Disappears completely; the surface looks like smooth satin or metal with at most a faint fine grain. It changes the shine only, never the colour. articles.title: Terrain Erosion
articles.summary: Broad soft roughness drift; ridgetops glossier, valleys duller, faint micro tooth. Plain smooth satin or metal; the specks disappear entirely.
articles.what: Eroded terrain topology — multi-octave domain-warped FBM, ridgetops lower roughness (wind-polished rock), valley floors higher roughness (sediment), cliff faces high meta Up close: Sparse tiny bright specks and short scratches, 1-4 px, scattered at random across the highlight on metallic; satin has only a couple. The broad ridge and valley drift in the description is not visible at 1:1, the surface looks smooth. From a distance: Plain smooth satin or metal; the specks disappear entirely. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Organic & Natural (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
